msm-methylsulfonylmethane: MSM, or methylsulfonylmethane, is an organic sulfur-containing compound found naturally in plants, animals and humans. Oral supplements are the most common form, and reported side effects include bloating, constipation, diarrhea, headaches and itching.
black-seed-oil: Black seed oil is extracted from the seeds of the Nigella sativa plant and has a long history in traditional medicine. It can be massaged into the scalp, and people with sensitive skin may mix it with a carrier oil to reduce the risk of irritation.
dandruff-cause-hair-thinning: Mild dandruff does not cause hair thinning or hair loss on its own, but inflammation and heavy scratching can damage follicles. Dandruff itself causes flakes and itchiness and is thought to come from an increase in a yeast fungus that feeds on scalp sebum.
lavender-oil-for-hair: Lavender oil is an essential oil extracted from lavender flowers by steam distillation. It should be diluted with a carrier oil before it goes on the skin, commonly 3 to 5 drops per tablespoon, to avoid irritation.
finasteride-results-timeline: Finasteride is an FDA-approved prescription medication for androgenetic alopecia, also called male pattern baldness. It blocks the 5-alpha-reductase enzyme that converts testosterone into DHT, and reported side effects include sexual dysfunction and mood changes.
butylene-glycol: Butylene glycol is a clear, odorless, water-soluble organic compound in the glycol family. It is used in cosmetic and personal care products, including hair care products, as a solvent, humectant and conditioning agent.
is-dimethicone-bad-for-hair: Dimethicone is a silicone-based polymer found in many hair and skin products, where it gives a smooth texture and helps lock in moisture. It forms a protective coating on hair strands that adds a glossy finish, makes detangling easier and helps reduce frizz.
ugly-hairlines: An uneven or receding hairline is one that looks imbalanced or lacks fullness, and it affects both men and women. Many people seek ways to get a fuller, more symmetrical hairline because it can influence how they feel about their appearance.
hemp-seed-oil: Hemp seed oil comes from the seeds of the Cannabis sativa plant and does not contain THC, the psychoactive compound in marijuana. It is rich in omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids, and first-time users are advised to patch test a small area of skin and wait 24 hours.
how-to-use-fully-vital-hair-serums: A scalp hair serum is a leave-in product applied to the scalp with a dropper and massaged in with the fingertips. It can be used on non-wash days, and it goes on towel-dried or dry hair, then stays in overnight.
shrinkage: Shrinkage is the reduction in hair length that happens when curly, coily or kinky hair dries or is manipulated. Wet hair stretches and looks longer, then retracts as it dries, and there is limited scientific research focused directly on shrinkage.
hair-botox-treatment: Hair botox is a cosmetic hair procedure used on hair that has been damaged by heat styling, chemical treatments and environmental stressors. Unlike botox for the skin, it does not involve injecting toxins, and it is often compared with keratin treatment.
low-level-laser-therapy: Low level laser therapy, also called red light or cold laser therapy, is a non-invasive procedure that uses low-level lasers or LEDs on the scalp. Individual responses can differ, so some people notice more of a change than others.
low-hairlines: A low hairline, also called a hairline recession, is one that starts unusually low on the forehead and gives the appearance of a smaller forehead area. It can affect self-confidence and make some people feel self-conscious about their appearance.
best-essential-oils: Essential oils are concentrated plant oils, and the main ones used in hair care are lavender, rosemary and peppermint. They are potent, so they should be diluted with a carrier oil and patch tested for skin sensitivities and allergies before use.
panthenol: Panthenol, also called provitamin B5, is a water-soluble ingredient derived from pantothenic acid and used in hair care products. It is generally well tolerated, though some people have mild allergies or sensitivities, so a patch test is recommended.
nutrafol-vs-fully-vital: Hair growth supplements are taken by mouth and contain vitamins and other ingredients chosen to support hair health. They are generally safe when used as directed, but individual reactions vary, so consult a healthcare provider if you have concerns.
citric-acid: Citric acid is an acid found naturally in citrus fruits that also takes part in the body's cellular energy production. It is generally safe in hair care products, but some people have mild irritation or allergic reactions, so a patch test is advised.
inflamed-hair-follicles: Inflamed hair follicles, also known as folliculitis, occur when hair follicles become irritated or infected. They can cause redness, swelling and discomfort, and they can happen anywhere on the body where hair grows, including the scalp and face.
papaya-extract: Papaya extract is made from papaya and contains vitamins A and C, minerals and enzymes such as papain. It is mostly safe for hair care, but people with sensitive skin or allergies should patch test, and overuse can irritate the scalp.
beta-sitosterol: Beta-sitosterol is a plant sterol found in the cell membranes of fruits, vegetables, nuts and seeds, and it is similar to cholesterol in humans. Research on its effects on hair is still evolving, and supplement users are advised to follow recommended dosages.
hair-cloning: Hair cloning is an experimental technique in which a small sample of a person's hair follicles would be multiplied in a laboratory and implanted back into the scalp. It is still in the research and development phase and is not yet widely available as a standard option.
early-receding-hairline: An early receding hairline is a condition in which hair begins to thin and recede at the front of the scalp earlier than expected. It can lead to a higher forehead and decreased hair density in that area.
organic-hair-serum: Organic hair serums are leave-in hair products made with plant-based ingredients. They are generally used after washing the hair and before styling, and overuse can leave residue on the hair, so the right amount matters.
bhringraj: Bhringraj is an herb long used in traditional Ayurvedic medicine and often called the king of herbs. Side effects are rare, but topical use can cause dermatitis or irritation where it is applied, and the oil is typically massaged into the scalp.
female-pattern-baldness: Female pattern baldness is a common hair loss condition in women that is caused by genetic, hormonal and other factors. According to the American Hair Loss Association, it can affect over 50% of women over the age of 50.
matcha-green-tea-extract: Matcha green tea extract is a concentrated form of green tea that contains vitamins A and C, zinc, selenium and the antioxidant EGCG. Direct research on matcha is more limited than research on green tea extract in general.
schisandra: Schisandra chinensis is a fruit-bearing vine native to parts of Asia, also called wu wei zi or the five-flavored berry. It is generally well tolerated, though high doses can cause mild digestive discomfort such as an upset stomach or loose stools.
how-to-use-fully-vital-products: Hair supplements and scalp serums are designed to be used together as one daily routine. The supplements are taken every day, and one or both serums are applied to the scalp every day.
finasteride: Finasteride is an FDA-approved medication primarily used for hair loss in men, and it belongs to the 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors, which inhibit the conversion of testosterone into DHT. It is approved for oral use, and reported side effects include headaches, dizziness and mild stomach discomfort.
burdock-root: Burdock root is the root of the burdock plant, a vegetable with an earthy, slightly sweet flavor that has a long history in traditional medicine. For hair, burdock root oil or extract can be massaged into the scalp or added to shampoo or conditioner.
derma-roller-for-beard: A derma roller, also called a microneedle roller, is a handheld device with hundreds of tiny needles that create microscopic punctures in the skin. Some people notice temporary redness, mild swelling or slight skin sensitivity afterward, which typically subsides within a few hours to a couple of days.
best-hair-growth-serum-for-black-hair: Hair serums are leave-in products applied to the hair and scalp, and the right one depends on your hair type and concerns. Results vary from person to person depending on genetics, overall health and hair care practices.
hair-mineral-analysis: Hair mineral analysis is a test that measures the mineral content of a hair sample, such as iron, zinc, copper and magnesium. The results are used to look for potential nutrient imbalances that may affect hair.
best-hair-growth-serum-for-blondes: Hair serums are leave-in products, and for light-colored hair they are applied after washing to clean, towel-dried, damp hair. Results differ from person to person, and people with oily or fine hair should use them sparingly or choose lightweight formulas.
vegamour-vs-fully-vital: Hair care brands are often compared on shelf life, performance in humidity, eco-friendliness, ingredient quality, product range and price. As with all hair care products, individual reactions vary, so a patch test is advisable, especially for sensitive skin.
formaldehyde: Formaldehyde is a naturally occurring organic compound made of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen that is widely used across industries. Some people experience scalp sensitivity to it, so a patch test is advised and products containing it should be used in a well-ventilated area.
fully-vital-reviews-dani: A health coach describes developing hair thinning while following a ketogenic diet and living with polycystic ovary syndrome, or PCOS. She used a three-month hair system every day and took before pictures.
shedavi-or-fully-vital: Hair vitamins are supplements designed to provide the nutrients hair needs. A possible side effect is an allergic reaction, so it is important to check the ingredient list for potential allergens before taking them.
androgenetic-alopecia: Androgenetic alopecia, commonly known as female pattern baldness, is a hereditary hair loss condition in women. It is characterized by gradual thinning and a widening part, and it results from genetic factors and the influence of androgens such as testosterone.
dextran: Dextran is a complex carbohydrate made of chains of glucose molecules, produced by bacteria or yeast fermenting sucrose. It is water-soluble, and in the food industry it is used as an additive and thickening agent that improves texture.
how-to-use-fully-vital-hair-supplements: Hair supplements are taken with your first meal of the day, and that meal should include some healthy fats. Some of the ingredients are water soluble and some are fat soluble, so fats increase the availability of the nutrients.
bimatoprost: Bimatoprost is a synthetic prostamide originally recognized for its use in ophthalmology, the branch of medicine concerned with the eye. The recommended dosage should be followed, and a missed application should not be made up by applying a double amount.
saw-palmetto: Saw palmetto is a palm native to the southeastern United States whose berries are sold as a dietary supplement, commonly in products for benign prostatic hyperplasia. Mild side effects can include stomach discomfort or headaches, and a healthcare professional should be consulted before starting any new supplement.
tea-tree-oil: Tea tree oil, also called melaleuca oil, is an essential oil derived from the leaves of the Melaleuca alternifolia tree, which is native to Australia. It is extracted by steam distillation, and a patch test with a diluted amount on the inner arm for 24 hours is advised before use.
keratolytic-agents: Keratolytic agents are ingredients that soften the keratin protein holding dead skin cells together so the cells can shed more easily. They are generally well tolerated, but they can cause mild redness, dryness or irritation, so a patch test is recommended.
derma-roller-for-hair-loss: A derma roller, also called a microneedling roller, is a handheld device with hundreds of tiny needles that create micro-injuries on the skin. After use, some people notice temporary redness, mild swelling or skin sensitivity.
hair-replacement: Hair replacement covers surgical and non-surgical procedures used where hair has thinned or balding has occurred. Like any surgical procedure, hair transplantation carries a slight risk of infection, and other side effects are typically mild and temporary.
pura-dor-vs-fully-vital: Hair growth supplements and serums list ingredients such as biotin, keratin, saw palmetto and niacin. Safety and ingredients are the main points of comparison, so check the ingredient list before choosing a product.
spoiled-child-hair-vs-fully-vital: The hair life cycle has three phases: anagen, the growth phase; catagen, the transition phase; and telogen, the resting phase. Ingredients commonly listed in hair growth products include biotin, keratin, vitamins and essential oils.
vital-proteins-or-fully-vital: Hair vitamins are supplements that supply nutrients for hair, and biotin is one of the common ingredients to look for. Always check ingredient lists for anything that might trigger allergies or sensitivities, and consider potential side effects.
best-hair-growth-serum-for-vibrant-hair: Red hair dyes often fade quickly, so vibrant colored hair needs extra care. Hair oil can be used on colored hair in moderation, and lightweight oils such as argan or jojoba oil avoid weighing hair down or causing greasiness.
viviscal-vs-fully-vital: Hair growth products are often compared on safety and allergy considerations, results over short-term and long-term use, quantity per use and availability. Application instructions vary by product, so follow the recommended usage on the packaging.
fully-vital-vs-thrive: Hair growth serums are products applied to the scalp, and they can be used on a dry or damp scalp depending on your preference and routine. It is not necessary to wash your hair every time before applying them.
castor-oil-for-hair-growth: Castor oil is a vegetable oil from the seeds of the Ricinus communis plant, made up mostly of ricinoleic acid. Scientific research on castor oil for hair is limited, and the evidence is mostly anecdotal.
moringa-extract: Moringa extract comes from the leaves of the Moringa oleifera tree, which is native to parts of Africa and Asia. The leaves contain vitamins A, C and E, and the tree is known for its rapid growth and drought resistance.
folate: Folate, also called vitamin B9, is a water-soluble vitamin the body cannot produce, so it must come from food or supplements. Food sources include leafy greens such as spinach and kale, legumes, citrus fruits, avocados and fortified cereals.
fade: A fade, as the term is used here, is a coloring technique that gradually blends hair from darker roots to lighter ends. It creates a seamless transition and is popular among people who prefer a subtle change and want to avoid abrupt color contrasts.
creatine-hair-loss: Scientific studies have not definitively shown a direct link between creatine supplements and hair loss, and the evidence is inconclusive. Hair loss is not a universally reported side effect of creatine, and genetics may affect how susceptible someone is.
thyroid-hair-loss: The thyroid gland in the neck regulates metabolism and energy production, and its hormones T3 and T4 influence many bodily functions. Those functions include the growth of hair, which is why thyroid imbalance is discussed in connection with hair loss.
7-daily-habits-that-damage-hair: Increased hair shedding in the shower or on the pillow is often what prompts people to look at their daily habits. One habit is the choice of hair products, whose ingredients such as parabens, phthalates, sodium laureth sulfate and artificial fragrances are typically used as emulsifiers, thickening agents and surfactants.
stem-cell-therapy: Stem cell therapy uses stem cells, the body's building blocks that can transform into various cell types, as a procedure in hair loss care. It can be relatively expensive, and side effects are rare but can include minor swelling or redness at the injection site.
derma-roller-for-hair: A derma roller, also called a microneedle roller, is a handheld device with hundreds of tiny needles that create micro-injuries on the skin. It was originally designed for skincare, and guidance is to use gentle pressure and avoid excessive force or vigorous rolling.
argan-oil: Argan oil is a natural oil extracted from the kernels of the argan tree, which is native to Morocco. It is high in vitamin E and essential fatty acids, and it is also rich in vitamins, minerals and antioxidants.
